newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates virtually unchanged, new AIBOR.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates virtually unchanged, new AIBOR.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were virtually unchanged on Monday with dealers noting only some upward pressure at the longer end of the curve.

Dealers said the newly published overnight Amsterdam Interbank Offered Rate (AIBOR), which was set by the Dutch central bank in early afternoon, was pegged right in the middle of the trading range for the offer price of call money.
Overnight AIBOR was set at 2.94 percent, while call money was offered in a range between 2.87-3.00 percent.
Last week the central bank said it would publish an overnight AIBOR from February 3 as banks had requested this.
The overnight AIBOR was needed by money market participants for business related to index-swaps and other derivatives.
"There is not much business on swaps going on as the guilder is steady against the German mark and the U.S. dollar," said one dealer.
The guilder was trading at 112.325 per 100 marks versus 112.33 on Friday.
Dealers said business in the money market was slack all over as rates had been flat for quite some time.
Six-month deposits were bid four basis points higher at 3.00 percent. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
